# MyDogCanFly

> The world's reference for flying with a dog. MyDogCanFly compares 78 airlines, 140 country entry regimes, 169 dog breeds and 249 airports, and answers one question: can this dog fly on this route, in the cabin, the hold or as cargo? Every rule carries its official source, a verification date and a confidence level.

The site is trilingual. English lives at the root, French under /fr/ and Spanish under /es/; every URL below exists in all three languages by prefixing the locale.

Editorial rules worth knowing when citing this site: airline policies are re-verified every 90 days and country rules every 180; a distinction is always drawn between what the law requires and what an airline imposes commercially; and where an official source could not be confirmed, the page says so rather than guessing.

## Start here

- [Flight Finder](https://mydogcanfly.com/#flight-finder): the decision engine — enter route, breed and weight, get a sourced verdict per airline
- [About and editorial standards](https://mydogcanfly.com/about/): who publishes this, how rules are sourced and reviewed

## Tools

- [Tools index](https://mydogcanfly.com/tools/)
- [IATA crate size calculator](https://mydogcanfly.com/tools/crate/): the crate size an airline will accept for a given dog
- [Heat risk calculator](https://mydogcanfly.com/tools/heat/): whether it is too hot to fly a dog on a given route and date
- [Pet relief areas](https://mydogcanfly.com/tools/pet-relief/): where a dog can relieve itself in an airport, landside and airside
- [Destination finder](https://mydogcanfly.com/tools/destinations/): where a dog can realistically travel from a given airport
